artifacts.synopsis: The Session of Grace PCA in Ohio excommunicated Travis and Sherylyn Dougherty for heresy (Trinitarian partialism) without separately establishing contumacy. Ohio Presbytery reversed the excommunication but failed to impose any new censure or remand the matter to Session; the SJC sustained the complaint in part, finding Presbytery correctly overturned the excommunication for lack of contumacy evidence but erred in leaving the guilty parties with no censure and in mandating the transfer of members to another church.

In this particular case, the actions of SWFP on May 8, 2007 effectively imposed the censure of admonition without due process (BCO 30-2).

artifacts.synopsis: Southwest Florida Presbytery erred when it read into its May 8, 2007 minutes the Shepherding Committee's report containing findings of sins and errors against TE Grady without due process, effectively imposing the censure of admonition without proper judicial procedure. The SJC sustained the complaint and directed the presbytery to expunge the Shepherding Committee report from its minutes.

artifacts.synopsis: Appeal by TE Paul W. Lee against Korean Southwest Presbytery's judgment finding him guilty of disobeying citations, rejecting admonitions, and other charges. The Standing Judicial Commission found KSWP erred on all issues through procedural violations including improper admonishment of judicial commission members mid-trial, failure to record trial proceedings, denial of cross-examination rights, and improper censure. Case remanded for retrial or dismissal.

artifacts.title: Confusing use of 'admonition' in non-judicial rebuke context

matches.evidence: The CCB cautioned that using 'admonish' and 'admonition' outside their technical judicial-censure meaning in BCO 30 could cause confusion when applied to actions against church officers.

artifacts.title: Informal versus formal admonition and due-process requirements under BCO 27-5

matches.evidence: The CCB distinguished informal admonition (ordinary relational correction) from formal judicial admonition, holding that the paragraph in question did not require BCO 27-5 due process.
